_doc: ABC Islands (Aruba/Curacao/Bonaire) demand anchors for the Navier destination-cluster proposal. Sourced volumes are real (year + source noted); fares/capture are model inputs flagged for the economics cascade, NOT yet sealed.
_method: broad-footprint-first: real tourism/cruise/dive/air volumes establish the demand floor pool; capture (~55% captive, FP-style, per Jaideep 24-Jun) and per-leg fares applied in the model step. null beats confidently-wrong.

aruba.stopover_note: 2019 baseline 1,117,663; 2024 above pre-COVID record (record years 2023-2025). Conservative round.
aruba.cruise_note: 2019 = 832,001 pax / 324 calls (Oranjestad). 2024 in same band, growing.
aruba.source: Aruba Tourism Authority / Aruba Ports Authority via tourismanalytics.com

curacao.source: Curacao Tourist Board (CTB) / Curacao Ports Authority (834,890 pax, +17.5%, 328 vessels) / TravelPulse / HVS

bonaire.source: Tourism Corporation Bonaire (182,181 stayover, record) / CBS Netherlands (359,000 cruise 2024) / CaribJournal (43% dive)
bonaire.note: World dive capital; Bonaire National Marine Park = zero-wake/silent mandate (textbook Navier use-case). Bonaire uses USD; special municipality of NL.

routes.curacao_aruba: at least 2x daily (Divi Divi) + EZ Air
routes.curacao_bonaire: high-frequency core route (Divi Divi + EZ Air)

inter_island_air_substitution_pool.note: Existing paid inter-island demand already moving by 19-seat turboprop = the direct substitution pool for Navier sea legs. Curacao<->Bonaire (grounded Pioneer II) and Curacao<->Aruba are the live air markets; Bonaire<->Aruba is thin (weekly) = roadmap.
inter_island_air_substitution_pool.source: Divi Divi Air / EZ Air / Wikipedia / Alternative Airlines

grounded_now_pioneer_ii.legs: intra-island transfers (cruise-port->beach/marina, airport->resort, Klein Bonaire, Klein Curacao)
